   161	/** The fields a facility read needs from one holder's `MPToken`. */
   162	export interface MPTokenState {
   163	  /** Public, plaintext MPT balance. Absent means zero. */
   164	  publicAmount: number;
   165	  /**
   166	   * ⚠ **The same value as a DECIMAL STRING, losslessly.**
   167	   * `MPTAmount` is a UINT64 and rippled serialises it as a string for that
   168	   * reason; `publicAmount` above rounds anything over 2^53. The number is kept
   169	   * because the facility does arithmetic on it and its values are small; **any
   170	   * surface that DISPLAYS the amount must use this field** (`CLAIMS.md` E-220,
   171	   * the same defect E-215 fixed on the issuer path and missed here).
   172	   */
   173	  publicAmountRaw: string;
   174	  /** 33-byte compressed ElGamal point, hex — absent until the holder Converts. */
   175	  holderEncryptionKey?: string;
   176	  confidentialBalanceSpending?: string;
   177	  confidentialBalanceInbox?: string;
   178	  /** Present as a JSON **string** when non-zero, absent when zero. */
   179	  confidentialBalanceVersion: number;
   180	  /**
   181	   * ⚠ **The issuer's mandatory decryption mirror.** `CLAIMS.md` P-9: no
   182	   * configuration removes it, so this field is present on every confidential
   183	   * balance and the issuer's ElGamal secret decrypts it.
   184	   *
   185	   * ⚠ **It is a DIFFERENT ciphertext from `confidentialBalanceSpending`, and
   186	   * assuming otherwise costs an afternoon** — measured 2026-08-28: the issuer
   187	   * key against the holder's spending ciphertext returns `rc=-1` from `mptool
   188	   * decrypt`, and against this field returns the balance.
   189	   *
   190	   * Added 2026-08-28 for architecture §6 step 8's issuer view. The facility
   191	   * never read it: it reconciles each party's OWN balance with that party's own
   192	   * key, which is a different question from what the issuer can see.
   193	   */
   194	  issuerEncryptedBalance?: string;
   195	  /** The optional auditor's mirror, present only if an auditor was named. */
   196	  auditorEncryptedBalance?: string;
   197	}

   204	  confidentialOutstandingAmountRaw: string;

   211	/**
   212	 * A pinned read.
   213	 *
   214	 * Two `"validated"` reads seconds apart land in **different ledgers** — E-103
   215	 * observed it live against the public cluster. The index is taken once and
   216	 * every later call carries that number, and every answer is checked to have
   217	 * come from it. That check is the part `REVIEW-016` found *"asked for and never
   218	 * checked"* in the Rust version.
   219	 */
   220	export class Snapshot {
   221	  constructor(
   222	    private readonly ledger: LoopbackLedger,
   223	    readonly index: number,
   224	  ) {}
   225	
   226	  private async pinned(method: string, params: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<any> {
   227	    let result: any;
   228	    try {
   229	      result = await this.ledger.call(method, { ...params, ledger_index: this.index });
   230	    } catch (e) {
   231	      // ⚠ **A "not found" is an answer, and it is checked like one.** `REVIEW-058`
   232	      // found this path returning before the index check below, so a negative
   233	      // answer naming ledger 43 read as `null` in a snapshot pinned to 42. The
   234	      // Rust reader closed the same gap in `REVIEW-016` round two
   235	      // (`signer/src/ledger.rs`, `ledger_entry`) and this one never got the fix:
   236	      // two readings of one obligation, drifting (`CLAIMS.md` E-141's shape).
   237	      // rippled 3.4.1 names `ledger_index` on `entryNotFound`, measured on
   238	      // Devnet 2026-10-19; an absence that names no ledger proves nothing.
   239	      if (
   240	        e instanceof LedgerRefusal &&
   241	        e.code === "REFUSED_LEDGER_ENTRY_MISSING" &&
   242	        e.answeredIndex !== this.index
   243	      ) {
   244	        throw new LedgerRefusal(
   245	          "REFUSED_LEDGER_TORN",
   246	          `${method} said "not found" from ledger ${e.answeredIndex ?? "(none named)"}, not the ` +
   247	            `pinned ${this.index}. An absence that cannot be placed in the pinned ledger is not ` +
   248	            `an answer about it`,
   249	        );
   250	      }
   251	      throw e;
   252	    }
   253	    const answered = Number(result.ledger_index ?? result.ledger_current_index ?? NaN);
   254	    if (answered !== this.index) {
   255	      throw new LedgerRefusal(
   256	        "REFUSED_LEDGER_TORN",
   257	        `${method} answered from ledger ${answered}, not the pinned ${this.index}. ` +
   258	          `A snapshot assembled from two ledgers is a state that never existed`,
   259	      );
   260	    }
   261	    return result;
   262	  }
   263	
   264	  async sequenceOf(address: string): Promise<number> {
   265	    const r = await this.pinned("account_info", { account: address });
   266	    return Number(r.account_data.Sequence);
   267	  }
   268	
   269	  /** Every field of one holder's position, or `null` if they hold no MPToken. */
   270	  async mptoken(address: string, issuanceId: string): Promise<MPTokenState | null> {
   271	    let r: any;
   272	    try {
   273	      r = await this.pinned("ledger_entry", {
   274	        mptoken: { mpt_issuance_id: issuanceId, account: address },
   275	      });
   276	    } catch (e) {
   277	      if (e instanceof LedgerRefusal && e.code === "REFUSED_LEDGER_ENTRY_MISSING") return null;
   278	      throw e;
   279	    }
   280	    const n = entryOfType(r, "MPToken");
   281	    return {
   282	      publicAmount: Number(n.MPTAmount ?? 0),
   283	      publicAmountRaw: String(n.MPTAmount ?? "0"),
   284	      holderEncryptionKey: n.HolderEncryptionKey,
   285	      confidentialBalanceSpending: n.ConfidentialBalanceSpending,
   286	      confidentialBalanceInbox: n.ConfidentialBalanceInbox,
   287	      confidentialBalanceVersion: Number(n.ConfidentialBalanceVersion ?? 0),
   288	      issuerEncryptedBalance: n.IssuerEncryptedBalance,
   289	      auditorEncryptedBalance: n.AuditorEncryptedBalance,
   290	    };
   291	  }
   292	
   293	  async issuance(issuanceId: string): Promise<IssuanceState> {
   294	    const r = await this.pinned("ledger_entry", { mpt_issuance: issuanceId });
   295	    const n = entryOfType(r, "MPTokenIssuance");
   296	    return {
   297	      issuer: n.Issuer,
   298	      // ⚠ **A JSON string, as rippled serialises every `UINT64`.** Reading it
   299	      // with a numeric helper sees every value as absent, and a preflight check
   300	      // that always passes looks identical to one that works. The signer has a
   301	      // control test for exactly this; so does `facility/tests`.
   302	      confidentialOutstandingAmount: Number(n.ConfidentialOutstandingAmount ?? 0),
   303	      confidentialOutstandingAmountRaw: String(n.ConfidentialOutstandingAmount ?? "0"),
   304	      issuerEncryptionKey: n.IssuerEncryptionKey,
   305	      auditorEncryptionKey: n.AuditorEncryptionKey,
   306	      transferFee: Number(n.TransferFee ?? 0),
   307	      flags: Number(n.Flags ?? 0),
   308	    };
   309	  }
   310	}
   311	
   312	/**
   313	 * The node must be the kind of object that was asked for. Without this a node
   314	 * could return an `MPTokenIssuance` where an `MPToken` was requested, and the
   315	 * reader would take whichever fields happened to have the right names. The Rust
   316	 * reader has checked this since `REVIEW-016`; this one did not until `REVIEW-058`.
   317	 */
   318	function entryOfType(r: any, expected: string): any {
   319	  const n = r?.node;
   320	  if (!n || typeof n !== "object") {
   321	    throw new LedgerRefusal("REFUSED_LEDGER_MALFORMED", `ledger_entry returned no node`);
   322	  }
   323	  if (n.LedgerEntryType !== expected) {
   324	    throw new LedgerRefusal(
   325	      "REFUSED_LEDGER_MALFORMED",
   326	      `ledger_entry was asked for a ${expected} and returned a ${String(n.LedgerEntryType ?? "(no LedgerEntryType)")}`,
   327	    );
   328	  }
   329	  return n;
   330	}

   454	  async call(method: string, params: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<any> {
   455	    // ⚠ **Every method that submits, not just `submit`.** It matched the exact

   483	/**

   485	 *
   486	 * ⚠ **Three refusals, not one.** An unset variable, a variable set to something
   487	 * else, and the accepted case are different situations and a caller who gets

   489	 * §3a B-VII is the standing reason: a refusal a client renders as "please try

   493	  const accepted = process.env.WCONF_ACCEPT_REMOTE_LEDGER_RISK;
   494	  if (accepted === RISK_ACCEPTANCE_PHRASE) {

   522	/**
   523	 * Whether two URLs name the same endpoint, ignoring the trailing slash `fetch`
   524	 * adds to `response.url`.
   525	 *
   526	 * Exported so the comparison can be tested directly: the path that reaches it
   527	 * in `rawCall` requires a runtime that ignores `redirect: "error"`, which is not
   528	 * a state a test can produce — and an untestable check is one nobody finds out
   529	 * is wrong until it fires in production, which is exactly what happened to its
   530	 * first version.
   531	 */
   532	export function sameEndpoint(a: string, b: string): boolean {
   533	  try {
   534	    return new URL(a).href === new URL(b).href;
   535	  } catch {
   536	    return false;
   537	  }
   538	}

   540	async function rawCall(
   541	  endpoint: string,
   542	  method: string,
   543	  params: Record<string, unknown>,
   544	): Promise<any> {
   545	  let response: Response;
   546	  try {
   547	    response = await fetch(endpoint, {
   548	      method: "POST",
   549	      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
   550	      body: JSON.stringify({ method, params: [params] }),
   551	      // ⚠ **A redirect is the loopback check undone.** `fetch` follows them by
   552	      // default; `307`/`308` preserve the method and body, so a loopback
   553	      // responder could forward this POST to a remote host and every later
   554	      // call with it. `error` makes the fetch reject instead.
   555	      redirect: "error",
   556	    });
   557	  } catch (e) {
   558	    throw new LedgerRefusal("REFUSED_LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE", `${method}: ${String(e)}`);
   559	  }
   560	  // Belt as well as braces: if a runtime ever honoured a redirect anyway, the
   561	  // response carries the final URL and it must be the one we asked.
   562	  //
   563	  // ⚠ **This compared against LOOPBACK-ness until the first run under the
   564	  // accepted-risk hatch, and that was wrong in both directions.** It refused
   565	  // every remote endpoint even when the risk had been accepted — which is how
   566	  // it was found, by running the artifact rather than by reading it — and it
   567	  // would have *accepted* a redirect from one loopback port to another. The
   568	  // invariant a redirect violates is "the answer came from where I asked", and
   569	  // that is what this checks now. `CLAIMS.md` E-139: running the artifact
   570	  // catches what a fix leaves standing.
   571	  if (response.url && !sameEndpoint(response.url, endpoint)) {
   572	    throw new LedgerRefusal(
   573	      "REFUSED_REDIRECTED",
   574	      `${method}: asked ${endpoint} and the answer came from ${response.url}. A redirect is ` +
   575	        `the endpoint check undone`,
   576	    );
   577	  }
   578	  if (!response.ok) {
   579	    throw new LedgerRefusal("REFUSED_LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE", `${method}: HTTP ${response.status}`);
   580	  }
   581	  const body: any = await response.json();
   582	  const result = body.result;
   583	  if (!result) throw new LedgerRefusal("REFUSED_LEDGER_MALFORMED", `${method}: no result`);
   584	  if (result.status === "error") {
   585	    // `entryNotFound` is an answer, not a failure — a holder who has not opted
   586	    // in has no `MPToken`, and the caller distinguishes that from a broken read.
   587	    const missing = result.error === "entryNotFound" || result.error === "objectNotFound";
   588	    const code = missing ? "REFUSED_LEDGER_ENTRY_MISSING" : "REFUSED_LEDGER_ERROR";
   589	    // The ledger a negative answer names travels with it, so `Snapshot` can
   590	    // check it like any other answer. `NaN` when the node named none.
   591	    const answered = missing ? Number(result.ledger_index ?? result.ledger_current_index ?? NaN) : undefined;
   592	    throw new LedgerRefusal(code, `${method}: ${result.error} ${result.error_message ?? ""}`, answered);
   593	  }
   594	  return result;
   595	}
   810	            }),
   811	            ledger_index,
   812	            "MPToken",
   813	            true,
   814	        )? {
   815	            Some(n) => n,
   816	            // Not opted in. The initialising Convert is what creates it, so

   865	    /// Read the destination's registered `HolderEncryptionKey`.

   869	    /// different one is the torn read this module exists to prevent.
   870	    ///
   871	    /// ⚠ **There is no local anchor on this value.** See the module header:

   873	    pub fn holder_encryption_key(
   874	        &self,
   875	        account: &str,
   876	        issuance_id: &[u8; 24],
   877	        ledger_index: u32,
   878	    ) -> Result<Option<[u8; 33]>, LedgerError> {
   879	        let Some(node) = self.ledger_entry(
   880	            json!({
   881	                "mptoken": { "mpt_issuance_id": xrpl::hex(issuance_id), "account": account },
   882	                "ledger_index": ledger_index
   883	            }),
   884	            ledger_index,
   885	            "MPToken",
   886	            true,
   887	        )?
   888	        else {
   889	            return Ok(None);
   890	        };
   891	        // ⚠ **The identity check matters most HERE.** This is the destination's
   892	        // key, the field with no local anchor and the one whose substitution
   893	        // leaks the amount rather than failing the transaction (F-23). A node
   894	        // answering with some other account's `MPToken` would otherwise be
   895	        // indistinguishable from an honest answer.
   896	        Self::mptoken_is_the_one_asked_for(&node, account, issuance_id)?;
   897	        field_hex::<33>(&node, "HolderEncryptionKey")
   898	    }
   899	
   900	    /// The returned `MPToken` must be **this account's, for this issuance**.
   901	    fn mptoken_is_the_one_asked_for(
   902	        node: &Value,
   903	        account: &str,
   904	        issuance_id: &[u8; 24],
   905	    ) -> Result<(), LedgerError> {
   906	        if node.get("Account").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some(account) {
   907	            return Err(LedgerError::Malformed(format!(
   908	                "an MPToken was requested for {account} and one for {:?} was returned",
   909	                node.get("Account")
   910	            )));
   911	        }
   912	        let want = xrpl::hex(issuance_id);
   913	        let got = node.get("MPTokenIssuanceID").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
   914	        if !got.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&want) {
   915	            return Err(LedgerError::Malformed(format!(
   916	                "an MPToken was requested for issuance {want} and one for `{got}` was returned"
   917	            )));
   918	        }
   919	        Ok(())
   920	    }
   921	
   922	    fn ledger_entry(
   923	        &self,
   924	        params: Value,
   925	        ledger_index: u32,
   926	        expect_type: &str,
   927	        tolerate_missing: bool,
   928	    ) -> Result<Option<Value>, LedgerError> {
   929	        let r = self.source.call("ledger_entry", params)?;
   930	        if let Some(e) = rpc_error("ledger_entry", &r) {
   931	            if tolerate_missing {
   932	                if let LedgerError::Rpc { error, .. } = &e {
   933	                    if error == "entryNotFound" {
   934	                        // ⚠ **`not found` is an answer, and it is checked like
   935	                        // one.** Round two of `REVIEW-016` found this path
   936	                        // returning `None` without ever asking which ledger
   937	                        // said so — which made the module's *"every answer must
   938	                        // say it came from the ledger that was asked for"* a
   939	                        // sentence with an exception in it. rippled carries
   940	                        // `ledger_index` and `validated` on the error response;
   941	                        // the live Devnet test drives this path.
   942	                        self.came_from("ledger_entry", &r, ledger_index)?;
   943	                        return Ok(None);
   944	                    }
   945	                }
   946	            }
   947	            return Err(e);
   948	        }
   949	        self.came_from("ledger_entry", &r, ledger_index)?;
   950	        let node = r
   951	            .get("node")
   952	            .cloned()
   953	            .ok_or_else(|| LedgerError::Malformed("ledger_entry returned no `node`".into()))?;
   954	        // The node must be the kind of object that was asked for. Without this
   955	        // a node could return an `MPTokenIssuance` where an `MPToken` was
   956	        // requested, and `field_hex` would read whichever fields happened to
   957	        // have the right names and lengths.
   958	        let kind = node.get("LedgerEntryType").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
   959	        if kind != expect_type {
   960	            return Err(LedgerError::Malformed(format!(
   961	                "ledger_entry was asked for a {expect_type} and returned a `{kind}`"
   962	            )));
   963	        }
   964	        Ok(Some(node))
   965	    }
   966	}

   206	function liveFiles(dir = "."): string[] {
   207	  const out: string[] = [];
   208	  for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
   209	    const p = join(dir, name);
   210	    if (EXEMPT_DIRS.some((d) => (p + "/").includes(d.replace(/^\.?\//, "")))) continue;
   211	    let st;
   212	    try { st = statSync(p); } catch { continue; }
   213	    if (st.isDirectory()) { out.push(...liveFiles(p)); continue; }
   214	    if (!LIVE_EXT.some((e) => p.endsWith(e))) continue;
   215	    if (EXEMPT_FILES.some((f) => p.endsWith(f))) continue;
   216	    out.push(p);
   217	  }
   218	  return out;
   219	}
   220	
   221	/**
   222	 * The REAL detector. Every control below calls THIS — a control that
   223	 * re-implements the check proves only that the re-implementation works
   224	 * (`CLAIMS.md` E-182).
   225	 */
   226	export function scan(extra?: { name: string; text: string }): Hit[] {
   227	  const bad: Hit[] = [];
   228	  const items: Array<[string, string]> = liveFiles().map((f) => [f, readFileSync(f, "utf8")]);
   229	  if (extra) items.push([extra.name, extra.text]);
   230	  for (const [file, text] of items) {
   231	    const lines = text.split("\n");
   232	    for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
   233	      for (const r of RETRACTED) {
   234	        if (!lines[i].includes(r.phrase)) continue;
   235	        const window = lines.slice(Math.max(0, i - WINDOW), i + WINDOW + 1).join("\n");
   236	        // ⚠⚠ **A RETRACTION TOKEN IS REQUIRED, NOT MERELY A CITATION —
   237	        // `CLAIMS.md` E-238.** E-232 tightened the marker LISTS after a review
   238	        // id forgave the assertion it was added to catch; the REVIEW-037
   239	        // spot-check proved the MODE survived that fix, because a bare
   240	        // `E-224` — an ordinary cross-reference that appears for a hundred
   241	        // unrelated reasons — still satisfied `markers.some()`.
   242	        //
   243	        // ⚠ **A citation says "this was discussed". A STRIKE says "this is
   244	        // withdrawn".** Only the second may forgive a live assertion, so a hit
   245	        // is now forgiven only when the window carries BOTH a retraction token
   246	        // AND one of the phrase's own markers.
   247	        // ⚠ The phrase's own marker lists CONTAIN the retraction tokens, so a
   248	        // naive `markers.some()` let a lone `RETRACTED` satisfy BOTH halves and
   249	        // the requirement was toothless. **Caught by this gate's own new
   250	        // control, before the fix was believed.** Identity and strike must come
   251	        // from disjoint sets.
   252	        const struck = RETRACTION_TOKENS.some((m) => window.includes(m));
   253	        const cited = r.markers
   254	          .filter((m) => !RETRACTION_TOKENS.includes(m))
   255	          .some((m) => window.includes(m));
   256	        if (!(struck && cited)) {
   257	          bad.push({ file, line: i + 1, phrase: r.phrase, why: r.why });
   258	        }
   259	      }
   260	    }
   261	  }
   262	  return bad;
   263	}
   264	
   265	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   266	
   267	if (import.meta.main) {
   268	  let failures = 0;
   269	  let controls = 0;
   270	  const control = (label: string, ok: boolean) => {
   271	    controls++;
   272	    console.log(`  CONTROL ${ok ? "✓" : "✗"} ${label}`);
   273	    if (!ok) failures++;
   274	  };
   275	
   276	  console.log("check-disclosure-phrases — no live file may assert a retracted disclosure");
   277	  console.log("  (docs/reviews/ is exempt: a packet is the record of what a leg was shown)\n");
   278	
   279	  // ⚠ A gate over an EMPTY set passes trivially and says nothing. Refuse first.
   280	  if (RETRACTED.length === 0) {
   281	    console.log("FAIL: the retracted-phrase list is empty — this gate would assert nothing");
   282	    process.exit(1);
   283	  }
   284	  console.log(`Scanning ${liveFiles().length} live files for ${RETRACTED.length} retracted phrases\n`);
   285	
   286	  const hits = scan();
   287	  if (hits.length) {
   288	    for (const h of hits) {
   289	      console.log(`  ⚠ ASSERTED: ${h.file}:${h.line} — "${h.phrase}"`);
   290	      console.log(`             ${h.why}`);
   291	    }
   292	    failures += hits.length;
   293	  } else {
   294	    console.log("  ✓ no live file asserts a retracted disclosure");
   295	  }
   296	
   297	  console.log("\nControls — each runs through the SAME detector the real check calls");
   298	  const p = RETRACTED[0];
   299	  control(
   300	    "an INJECTED retracted phrase with no correction marker IS caught",
   301	    scan({ name: "<injected>", text: `prose\n${p.phrase}\nmore prose` }).some((h) => h.file === "<injected>"),
   302	  );
   303	  control(
   304	    "the SAME phrase with a retraction TOKEN and its marker is NOT caught",
   305	    !scan({ name: "<injected>", text: `⚠ RETRACTED, ${p.markers[0]}:\n~~${p.phrase}~~\n` }).some((h) => h.file === "<injected>"),
   306	  );
   307	  // ⚠⚠ E-238. A citation is not a retraction. This is the mode E-232's fix left
   308	  // open, demonstrated by the REVIEW-037 spot-check with an unrelated `E-224`.
   309	  control(
   310	    "a BARE CITATION with no retraction token does NOT forgive the hit",
   311	    scan({ name: "<injected>", text: `⚠ see ${p.markers[0]} for background\n${p.phrase}\n` }).some((h) => h.file === "<injected>"),
   312	  );
   313	  control(
   314	    "a retraction TOKEN alone, without the phrase's own marker, does NOT forgive",
   315	    scan({ name: "<injected>", text: `⚠ RETRACTED elsewhere\n${p.phrase}\n` }).some((h) => h.file === "<injected>"),
   316	  );
   317	  control(
   318	    "a marker OUTSIDE the window does NOT forgive the hit",
   319	    scan({
   320	      name: "<injected>",
   321	      text: `${p.markers[0]}\n${"filler\n".repeat(WINDOW + 2)}${p.phrase}\n`,
   322	    }).some((h) => h.file === "<injected>"),
   323	  );
   324	  control(
   325	    "clean prose is NOT caught",
   326	    scan({ name: "<injected>", text: "nothing retracted here at all\n" }).length === hits.length,
   327	  );
   328	  control(
   329	    "EVERY phrase in the list is detectable, not just the first",
   330	    RETRACTED.every((r) =>
   331	      scan({ name: "<injected>", text: r.phrase }).some((h) => h.file === "<injected>"),
   332	    ),
   333	  );
   334	
   335	  console.log("\n" + "-".repeat(74));
   336	  if (failures) {
   337	    console.log(`FAIL: ${hits.length} asserted retraction(s), ${failures - hits.length} control failure(s).`);
   338	    console.log("⚠ A retracted claim is standing in a live file. Grep the PHRASE, not the line.");
   339	    process.exit(1);
   340	  }
   341	  console.log(
   342	    `PASS: no live file asserts any of ${RETRACTED.length} retracted disclosures — under ${controls} controls,\n` +
   343	      "      each running through the same detector the real check calls.",
   344	  );
   345	  console.log("⚠ LEXICAL, over a NAMED SET. It catches COPIES, not paraphrases, and it");
   346	  console.log("  cannot tell whether a claim is true. See the header for what it does not say.");
   347	}

    68	function fakeNode(handler: (method: string, params: any) => any) {
    69	  const server = Bun.serve({
    70	    hostname: "127.0.0.1",
    71	    port: 0,
    72	    async fetch(req) {
    73	      const body: any = await req.json();
    74	      const result = handler(body.method, body.params?.[0] ?? {});
    75	      return Response.json({ result: { status: "success", ...result } });
    76	    },
    77	  });
    78	  return { server, endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:${server.port}` };
    79	}

     6	  loader: async () => {
     7	    // ⚠ Loaders read. There is no server function here and none may be added
     8	    // that reaches a signing operation — ADR-0003 D3 names that as exactly the
     9	    // one-line mechanism to watch for.
    10	    // ⚠ Identity is asserted in the ROOT route's beforeLoad, so it covers every

    57	      <Panel title="What it never claims" tone="warn">
    58	        <ul className="text-sm space-y-2">
    59	          {(meta.neverClaims ?? []).map((i: any) => (
    60	            <li key={i.rule}>
    61	              <code className="text-xs font-semibold mr-2 opacity-70">{i.rule}</code>
    62	              {i.text}
    63	            </li>
    64	          ))}
    65	        </ul>
    66	        <p className="text-xs opacity-60 mt-3">
    67	          These are CLAIMS.md rows cited, not restated. A second copy of a claim is a second thing
    68	          to go stale.
    69	        </p>
    70	      </Panel>
    71	
    72	      <Panel title="Signer">
    73	        {signer.reachable ? (
    74	          <div className="text-sm space-y-1">
    75	            <div><span className="opacity-60">version</span> <code>{signer.status.version}</code></div>
    76	            <div><span className="opacity-60">note</span> {signer.status.note}</div>
    77	          </div>
    78	        ) : (
    79	          <p className="text-sm opacity-70">
    80	            Not reachable: {signer.reason ?? signer.error}. This is a named gap, not a failure — the
    81	            tier is read-only and every ledger view is complete without it.
    82	          </p>
    83	        )}
    84	        <p className="text-xs opacity-60 mt-3">{signer.whatThisIs}</p>
    85	        <p className="text-xs opacity-60 mt-1">{signer.whatThisIsNot}</p>
    86	      </Panel>
    87	    </>
    88	  );
    89	}

    10	/**
    11	 * Prove-and-contrast. ⚠ The contrast is the lesson: a browser wallet cannot
    12	 * hold a confidential position, and the reasons are structural rather than
    13	 * missing features.
    14	 */
    15	function Wallet() {
    16	  const { rows, namedGaps } = Route.useLoaderData();
    17	  const wallet = rows.find((r: any) => r.id === "browser-wallet");
    18	
    19	  return (
    20	    <>
    21	      <Panel title="A browser wallet cannot hold a confidential position">
    22	        <p className="text-sm leading-relaxed mb-4">
    23	          This is not a feature gap in the three wallet APIs examined (Xaman, GemWallet,
    24	          Crossmark, checked 2026-08-28). ⚠ It is <em>not</em> a claim that no wallet API
    25	          could ever close it — an extension that derived or held an ElGamal key internally,
    26	          and exposed a prove-and-sign operation without exporting seed material, would.
    27	          Nothing observed does. Three reasons, each structural to the design as it stands:
    28	        </p>
    29	        <ol className="text-sm space-y-3 list-decimal pl-5">
    30	          <li>
    31	            A confidential operation needs <strong>two</strong> secrets — the ElGamal secret, to
    32	            decrypt the balance and produce the proof, and the XRPL account key, to sign. A wallet
    33	            supplies the second.
    34	          </li>
    35	          <li>
    36	            Under the ruled key generation, the ElGamal secret is <strong>derived from the master
    37	            seed</strong>. There is no other way to obtain it for a derived-key account.
    38	          </li>
    39	          <li>
    40	            A wallet extension exists <strong>in order not to release seed material</strong>. That is
    41	            the product, not a limitation of its API.
    42	          </li>
    43	        </ol>
    44	        <p className="text-sm mt-4">
    45	          So the operation cannot be assembled at all. The wallet is not being denied permission —
    46	          there is nothing to grant.
    47	        </p>
    48	      </Panel>
    49	
    50	      <Panel title="What a wallet CAN do">
    51	        <div className="text-sm space-y-3">
    52	          <div className="flex gap-3 items-start">
    53	            <Verdict v={wallet.publicTransactions.verdict} />
    54	            <div>
    55	              <div className="font-medium">Ordinary XRPL transactions</div>
    56	              <p className="opacity-80">{wallet.publicTransactions.detail}</p>
    57	              <p className="text-xs opacity-50 mt-1">{wallet.publicTransactions.citation}</p>
    58	            </div>
    59	          </div>
    60	          <div className="flex gap-3 items-start">
    61	            <Verdict v="yes" />
    62	            <div>
    63	              <div className="font-medium">Prove control of an account</div>
    64	              <p className="opacity-80">
    65	                Which is enough to show that account’s observer view — the same view anyone with the
    66	                address can read.
    67	              </p>
    68	            </div>
    69	          </div>
    70	        </div>
    71	      </Panel>
    72	
    73	      <Panel title="What this page does not claim" tone="warn">
    74	        <p className="text-sm">{namedGaps.walletCodec}</p>
    75	        <p className="text-xs opacity-60 mt-3">
    76	          CLAIMS.md E-206. Recorded because an earlier draft of this project’s reasoning led with
    77	          exactly this point, and it is a version fact an upstream release could close at any time.
    78	          The three reasons above cannot be closed by a codec release. A wallet that held the
    79	          viewing key and produced the proofs itself would close them, and none observed does.
    80	        </p>
    81	      </Panel>
    82	    </>
    83	  );
    84	}

     6	export const Route = createFileRoute("/issuer")({
     7	  validateSearch: (s: Record<string, unknown>) => ({
     8	    account: (s.account as string) ?? "",
     9	    issuanceId: (s.issuanceId as string) ?? "",
    10	  }),

    14	    if (!deps.account || !deps.issuanceId) return { picker, view: null };
    15	    const view = await api.issuer(deps.account, deps.issuanceId).catch((e) => ({ error: String(e) }));
    16	    return { picker, view };
    17	  },
    18	  component: Issuer,
    19	});

    21	function Issuer() {
    22	  const { picker, view } = Route.useLoaderData();
    23	  const search = Route.useSearch();
    24	
    25	  return (
    26	    <>
    27	      <Panel title="A holder is never private from the issuer" tone="warn">
    28	        <p className="text-sm leading-relaxed">
    29	          The issuer’s decryption mirror is part of the protocol. No configuration removes it, and
    30	          no key source changes it. This page exists because showing what the issuer sees is the
    31	          honest counterpart to showing what the public sees — a demo of the happy path is not
    32	          evidence of confidentiality.
    33	        </p>
    34	        <p className="text-xs opacity-60 mt-3">CLAIMS.md P-9.</p>
    35	      </Panel>
    36	
    37	      <Panel title="Choose an account">
    38	        <AccountPicker to="/issuer" accounts={picker.accounts ?? []} current={search} />
    39	      </Panel>
    40	
    41	      <Panel title="Where the decryption happened" tone="warn">
    42	        <p className="text-sm leading-relaxed">
    43	          Not here. This page reads a file produced by a command-line tool that holds the issuer key
    44	          and decrypts a fixed set of accounts. ⚠ <strong>There is no request on this site that
    45	          reaches a decryption</strong>, so there is no oracle to authenticate — an earlier version
    46	          decrypted per request and that was a defect, not a feature.
    47	        </p>
    48	      </Panel>
    49	
    50	      <Panel title="Key handling">
    51	        <p className="text-sm">
    52	          {/* ⚠ The fallback fires before an account is picked, and it said the
    53	              web process reads the issuer key from its environment — false
    54	              since the snapshot design, and contradicting /api/meta's
    55	              holdsKeys:false on the same site (CLAIMS.md E-215). */}
    56	          {view?.keyPolicy ??
    57	            "This process holds no issuer key and performs no decryption. A command-line tool holds the key, decrypts a fixed set of accounts and writes results; this page reads those results. There is no request here that reaches a decryption."}
    58	        </p>
    59	      </Panel>
    60	
    61	      {view && !("error" in view) && (
    62	        <Panel title="Issuer view" tone={view.available ? "warn" : "plain"}>
    63	          {view.available ? (
    64	            <>
    65	              <div className="text-sm space-y-1">
    66	                <div>
    67	                  <span className="opacity-60">issuer decryption</span>{" "}
    68	                  <code className="text-base font-semibold">
    69	                    {view.decryptable ? "SUCCEEDED" : "not available"}
    70	                  </code>{" "}
    71	                  <span className="opacity-60">— the figure is withheld</span>
    72	                </div>
    73	                <div className="opacity-70">
    74	                  read from <code>{view.mirrorField}</code>, searched [0, {view.searchedTo}]
    75	                </div>
    76	                <div className="opacity-70">
    77	                  ⚠ The decrypted balance is <strong>not served by this tier</strong>. Loopback is
    78	                  not scoped to your user account, so an unauthenticated response would hand it to
    79	                  every local process — out of a file the producing tool writes{" "}
    80	                  <code>mode 0600</code>. To see the figure, run the CLI:{" "}
    81	                  <code>bun run tools/issuer-decrypt-balance.ts</code>.
    82	                </div>
    83	                {view.publicAmount !== undefined && (
    84	                  <div className="opacity-70">
    85	                    public plaintext MPT balance <code>{view.publicAmount}</code> — ⚠ a different
    86	                    number and a different thing; do not read one as the other
    87	                  </div>
    88	                )}
    89	              </div>
    90	              <p className="text-sm mt-3">
    91	                ⚠ The observer view shows this same holder’s balance as an opaque ciphertext. It was
    92	                read with one key that the protocol requires to exist.
    93	              </p>
    94	              {view.snapshotAgeNote && (
    95	                <p className="text-xs opacity-60 mt-2">
    96	                  {view.snapshotAgeNote}
    97	                  {view.snapshotAtUnix
    98	                    ? ` Taken ${new Date(view.snapshotAtUnix * 1000).toISOString()}.`
    99	                    : ""}
   100	                </p>
   101	              )}
   102	            </>
   103	          ) : (
   104	            <p className="text-sm">{view.reason}</p>
   105	          )}
   106	          <p className="text-sm mt-3">{view.whatThisProves}</p>
   107	        </Panel>
   108	      )}
   109	      {view && "error" in view && <Panel title="Read failed"><p className="text-sm">{String(view.error)}</p></Panel>}
   110	    </>
   111	  );

     1	/**
     2	 * The capability matrix — architecture §6 step 8's spine.
     3	 *
     4	 * **What each key source can and cannot do, and why.** Every cell carries a
     5	 * citation, and `web/api/capability.test.ts` checks that each citation
     6	 * RESOLVES AND EXISTS — that the named file, register row, ADR or ruling is
     7	 * there.
     8	 *
     9	 * ⚠⚠ **IT DOES NOT CHECK SEMANTIC SUPPORT, AND THIS COMMENT SAID IT DID UNTIL
    10	 * 2026-09-04** (*"says what the cell claims"*, `CLAIMS.md` E-239). **A citation
    11	 * to an existing but irrelevant file passes.** That is the exact shape this
    12	 * project claims discipline against — a gate asserting more than it checks —
    13	 * and it was found by an adversarial leg asked for the worst overclaim in the
    14	 * repository.
    15	 *
    16	 * ⚠ **This is DERIVED from the signer's own types, not restated from a
    17	 * handover table.** `KeySource` in `signer/src/onboarding.rs:274` has exactly
    18	 * two variants — `DerivedFromMasterSeed` and `Standalone` — and an absent
    19	 * `elgamal_key_source` reads as `standalone` rather than being upgraded
    20	 * (`holder.rs:53`). The browser-wallet row is the one that does **not** exist
    21	 * in the code, and saying so is the point of the row.
    22	 *
    23	 * ⚠ **`CLAIMS.md` P-4, P-9 and P-11 govern every sentence here.** This system
    24	 * hides amounts. It does not hide who transacts, with whom, when or how often,
    25	 * and no configuration makes a holder private from the issuer.
    26	 */
    27	
    28	export type Verdict = "yes" | "no" | "conditional" | "unverified";
    29	
    30	export interface Capability {
    31	  verdict: Verdict;
    32	  /** One sentence. Rendered as-is; it is a disclosure surface. */
    33	  detail: string;
    34	  /** Where the claim comes from. A file, a ruling, or a `CLAIMS.md` row. */
    35	  citation: string;
    36	}
    37	
    38	export interface KeySourceRow {
    39	  id: string;
    40	  label: string;
    41	  /** The token an operator writes into a holder profile, or null if none exists. */
    42	  profileToken: string | null;
    43	  existsToday: { built: boolean; where: string };
    44	  decryptOwnBalance: Capability;
    45	  proveAndSign: Capability;
    46	  publicTransactions: Capability;
    47	  /** The ruled disclosure this source obliges, if any. */
    48	  ruledDisclosure: string | null;
    49	}

    52	 * ⚠ **`REVIEW-012` condition 2 is RULED, not optional**, and it is the reason
    53	 * the derived rows carry a disclosure the standalone row does not. It must
    54	 * reach the holder **before the seed is asked for**.
    55	 */
    56	export const MASTER_SEED_DISCLOSURE =
    57	  "The master seed becomes a permanent decryption credential. Anyone who ever " +
    58	  "holds it can decrypt every confidential balance this account has held, past " +
    59	  "and future. XLS-96 has no key rotation and no key recovery (CLAIMS.md P-10), " +
    60	  "so this cannot be undone by rotating anything.";

    62	/**
    63	 * ⚠ **Issue #10 is OPEN and no code discharges it.** The derivation is
    64	 * specified in one repository document and is not a published standard.
    65	 */
    66	/**
    67	 * ⚠ **A NAMED GAP, and it is deliberately NOT one of the reasons the wallet row
    68	 * says no.** `CLAIMS.md` E-206: whether a given wallet build's bundled codec can
    69	 * serialise the XLS-0096 types is **not determinable from any published
    70	 * source** — the page-side SDKs (`@crossmarkio/sdk@0.4.0`, `@gemwallet/api@3.8.0`,
    71	 * `xumm@1.8.0`) carry no codec dependency at all, so serialisation happens
    72	 * inside a closed extension bundle whose version nobody publishes.
    73	 *
    74	 * ⚠ **It is excluded from the reasoning on purpose.** It is a version fact an
    75	 * upstream release can close at any time; the three reasons the row DOES give
    76	 * are structural and no wallet update can close them. A demonstration resting
    77	 * on this one would be falsified by a release note.
    78	 */
    79	export const WALLET_CODEC_GAP =
    80	  "Not determined: whether any given wallet build can serialise XLS-0096 transaction types. " +
    81	  "The page-side SDKs carry no codec dependency, so serialisation happens inside the extension " +
    82	  "and no vendor publishes that version. ⚠ This is NOT why a wallet cannot hold a confidential " +
    83	  "position — the reasons above are structural, and this one is a version fact that could change " +
    84	  "with any release. Determining it would need testing against a live extension build.";

   214	 * ⚠ **These are `CLAIMS.md` rows CITED, not restated.** A second copy of a

   218	export const INVARIANTS = [
   219	  { rule: "P-4", text: "No key source hides identities. Sender and receiver are public on every confidential transaction." },
   220	  { rule: "P-9", text: "No key source makes a holder private from the issuer. The issuer's decryption mirror is mandatory." },
   221	  { rule: "P-10", text: "No key source supports rotation or recovery. XLS-96 supports neither, at any level." },
   222	  { rule: "P-11", text: "No key source hides who transacts, when, or how often. Only amounts are hidden." },

     1	/**
     2	 * The web tier's ledger reads — **the facility's path, not a second one.**
     3	 *
     4	 * `facility/src/loopback.ts` already carries B-15's obligation: it refuses a
     5	 * non-loopback endpoint *before it connects*, it demands the risk-acceptance
     6	 * sentence by name when the owner's amendment is in force, it refuses any
     7	 * network but Devnet, and its `Snapshot` pins one validated index and checks
     8	 * every answer came from it (E-103). ⚠ **Reimplementing any of that here would
     9	 * produce a second reading of one obligation and the two would drift** — which
    10	 * is `CLAIMS.md` E-141's shape. This module composes it instead.
    11	 *
    12	 * ⚠ **What a wrong read costs is a CONFIDENTIALITY break, not a rejected
    13	 * transaction** (`CLAIMS.md` F-23, executed on 2026-08-19). That is why the
    14	 * endpoint discipline is inherited rather than relaxed for a read-only tier:
    15	 * the tier does not sign, but the values it *renders* are what a reader
    16	 * believes, and a substituted key renders a lie.
    17	 */

    25	export interface SourceDisclosure {
    26	  endpoint: string;
    27	  isLoopback: boolean;

    29	  buildVersion: string;

    31	  underB15Conditions: boolean;
    32	  note: string;

    36	  private constructor(
    37	    private readonly ledger: LoopbackLedger,
    38	    readonly disclosure: SourceDisclosure,

    41	  static async open(endpoint = process.env.WCONF_LEDGER_ENDPOINT ?? "http://127.0.0.1:5005"): Promise<LedgerView> {
    42	    const ledger = await LoopbackLedger.open(endpoint);
    43	    const id = ledger.identity;
    44	    return new LedgerView(ledger, {
    45	      endpoint: ledger.endpoint,
    46	      isLoopback: id.isLoopback,
    47	      networkId: id.networkId,

    52	        : "⚠ REMOTE ledger source, under the project owner's named risk acceptance (CLAIMS.md E-151). " +
    53	          "B-15's step-7 condition is NOT met and this view is not evidence about it. A hostile node " +
    54	          "substitutes a key just as well over TLS (CLAIMS.md F-23).",
    55	    });
    56	  }

    18	## Findings on the frozen commit
    19	
    20	`S-n | grade | claim | evidence | smallest fix`
    21	
    22	- **S-1 | MEDIUM | The page may never HOLD a secret, but nothing says it may never
    23	  ASK for one.** The may-never-touch list and the gate cover a seed or key in the
    24	  shipped output. A public page carrying this project's name, whose capability
    25	  matrix discusses master seeds, is the obvious shape for a phishing copy, and a
    26	  later page that "tells a visitor how to run the signer locally" (launch plan
    27	  phase 2 step 3) is one careless form away from inviting a paste. | ADR-0004
    28	  *What the hosted surface may touch*; launch plan phase 2 step 3 | Add *"never
    29	  asks a visitor for a seed, key or secret, in any input"* to the never-touch
    30	  list, step 9's falsifier and the gate.
    31	- **S-2 | MEDIUM | The shipped bundle is a distribution of third-party code, and
    32	  its licence notices are priced nowhere.** Phase 1's `NOTICE` and
    33	  `docs/third-party/INVENTORY.md` cover the repository's tracked text. A static
    34	  build ships React, TanStack, `@noble/curves`, `ripple-address-codec` and their
    35	  dependencies as minified code on a public URL, and the MIT and ISC licences
    36	  require their notices to travel with a copy. The ADR calls the output *"the
    37	  static output of the public repository's own source"*, which is also inexact
    38	  for the same reason. | ADR-0004 *Why this shape*; `NOTICE` | Name the bundle's
    39	  notices as a build requirement, and say *"built from the public repository and
    40	  its locked dependencies"*.
    41	- **S-3 | MEDIUM | The host can add script to a page, and the falsifier does not
    42	  name it.** Step 9 is falsified if the page ships bytes other than the gated
    43	  ones, and the never-touch list excludes third-party script. A host that injects
    44	  its own script into some deployments, a preview toolbar for example, would
    45	  violate both without any change of ours. Whether Vercel does this for a
    46	  prebuilt production deployment was **not checked**. | ADR-0004 D-H4; step 9's
    47	  *Falsified if* | Make phase 2 step 5's live check compare the served HTML with
    48	  the gated output, and name host injection as what it is looking for.
    49	- **S-4 | LOW | D-H2's first sentence says more than the design guarantees.**
    50	  *"No amount can be published because of it"* is true of the page, which cannot
    51	  sign. It is not true of a reader who copies a displayed `HolderEncryptionKey`
    52	  into their own tooling: a lying node then reaches F-23 through the reader. |
    53	  ADR-0004 D-H2 | *"Nothing on this page signs or submits. Do not use a value
    54	  shown here to build a transaction."*
    55	- **S-5 | LOW | D-H2's "Do not accept" row implies H3 escapes the acceptance.** H3
    56	  still reads one node, once, at build time, and a lying node then bakes wrong
    57	  values into every page. It changes when the risk is taken, not whether. |
    58	  ADR-0004 D-H2 table | Say H3 moves the read to build time and still needs the
    59	  first sentence.
    60	- **S-6 | LOW | D-H4 option A prices the token as a cost and not as a
    61	  credential.** A Vercel token on the owner's machine can replace what the public
    62	  page says, which is the same kind of power D8 exists to fence for the
    63	  repository. Its scope and expiry are not named. | ADR-0004 D-H4 | Name a token
    64	  scoped to the one project, with an expiry, kept where D8's export folder is.
    65	- **S-7 | LOW | Where the Content Security Policy lives is not said.** For a
    66	  prebuilt static deployment it is either a response header in the build

    71	        const node = entries[key];
    72	        if (!node) {
    73	          return Response.json({ result: { status: "error", error: "entryNotFound", ledger_index: 4_800_000, validated: true } });
    74	        }
    75	        const LedgerEntryType = key === "ISSUANCE" ? "MPTokenIssuance" : "MPToken";
    76	        return Response.json({ result: { status: "success", ledger_index: 4_800_000, node: { LedgerEntryType, ...node } } });
    77	      }
    78	      return Response.json({ result: { status: "error", error: "unknown" } });
    79	    },
    80	  });
    81	  return { server, endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:${server.port}` };
    82	}
    83	
    84	function tempBook() {
    85	  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "wconf-facility-"));
    86	  return {
    87	    book: FacilityBook.open(join(dir, "book.json"), ISSUANCE),
    88	    cleanup: () => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }),
    89	  };
    90	}

    92	const party = (label: string, seed: string): Party => ({
    93	  label,
    94	  seed,
    95	  address: addressOfSeed(seed),
    96	});

    98	async function facilityWith(entries: Record<string, any>, dedicatedSeed = SEED_B) {
    99	  const { server, endpoint } = nodeWith(entries);
   100	  const ledger = await LoopbackLedger.open(endpoint);
   101	  const { book, cleanup } = tempBook();
   102	  const bank = party("bank", SEED_A);
   103	  const dedicated = party("dedicated", dedicatedSeed);
   104	  const facility = new Facility(ledger, new FailHardSubmitter(ledger), book, {
   105	    issuanceId: ISSUANCE,
   106	    bank,
   107	    dedicated,
   108	    fullRange: 100_000,
   109	    ledgerEndpoint: endpoint,
   110	    workRoot: "/tmp/wconf-facility-test",
   111	    autoConfirm: true,
   112	    quietSigner: true,
   113	  });
   114	  return {
   115	    facility,
   116	    bank,
   117	    dedicated,
   118	    book,
   119	    stop: () => {
   120	      server.stop(true);
   121	      cleanup();
   122	    },
   123	  };
   124	}

   126	describe("construction", () => {
   127	  test("refuses a Dedicated Account that is the issuer — a PROTOCOL rule, not a preference", async () => {
   128	    // An issuer cannot convert its own issuance into a confidential balance;
   129	    // the ledger refuses it outright. That is the reason this design has a
   130	    // separate account at all, and stating it as a style choice would be a
   131	    // claim about rippled that rippled does not make.

   197	describe("the ElGamal key each party reads its own balance with", () => {

   240	   - **D3 — TanStack Start is kept, and the split is what makes it safe.** The capital-markets case is multi-role — issuer, auditor, supplier, facility operator, holder — and file-based routing with loaders is what lets those grow without a rewrite. SSR crosses no *new* boundary, because Elysia is already a local process reading holder data. ⚠ **The caveat makes the gate matter MORE, not less: server functions are exactly the one-line mechanism by which a later session adds a signing call.** Only the Elysia process may open the socket.
   241	   - **D4 — Ripple Custody is a research document and a simulated demo mode**, never an integration. This repository holds **no** Metaco Harmonize primary sources; every Harmonize specific is a dated named gap.
   242	
   243	   **What this step may touch:** public ledger state at a pinned validated index; the observer harness's view; the issuer-view decryption tool's output, given a demo issuer key handled as the secret it is; `Request::Status`; the facility's run records; and this repository's own documents.
   244	
   245	   **What it may never touch:** `Request::Pair`, `Request::Prepare`, any private key, any seed, any proof generation, and the Unix socket from anywhere but the Elysia process.
   246	
   247	   ⚠ **One thing verified at source during scoping, because D1's safety argument quotes it.** `signer/src/protocol.rs` documents `Status` as *"Public ledger read. Needs no grant and touches no secret."* **The second sentence is true and the first is false**: the handler at `signer/src/session.rs:248` reads **no ledger at all**. It returns the crate version, a hardcoded `keys_loaded: true`, and a note carrying the holder's address, the randomness ledger's generation id and its **entry count**. ⚠ **None of that is a secret and ⚠⚠ ~~none of it exceeds what the protocol already publishes~~ **STRUCK 2026-09-04, `CLAIMS.md` E-239 — the entry count includes cancelled confirmations, failed proofs and aborted attempts (`store.rs:753-756`), which no observer can reconstruct, and the API also returned the local socket path.** ⚠ E-241 withheld both on 2026-09-05; this said *"returns"* until 2026-10-18. P-4 and P-11 leave *who transacts and how often* public and publish neither of those — **but a comment that misdescribes what a call does is how E-200's secret went unwiped**, and this one sits under the sentence a ruling rests on. Corrected at the source rather than argued around (`CLAIMS.md` **E-205**).
   248	
   249	   **The gate is the load-bearing artifact of this step, and it is built before the UI.** `tools/check-web-readonly.ts`, wired into the `Makefile` beside the other six, asserting that no file under the web application imports a UDS client or names the socket path, that the Elysia process constructs `Status` and never `Pair` or `Prepare`, and that no route, loader or server function reaches a signing operation. ⚠ **Gates in this repository have been built to catch false passes and have false-passed** (E-165, E-168, E-182, E-198, E-203), so this one is verified by breaking it in both directions, its controls run through the real detector, and it **states what it does not check** in its own output.
   250	
   251	   **The capability matrix is the spine of the demonstration, not a footnote**, and it is derived from what the code supports rather than restated from a handover table. ⚠ **The `derived-from-master-seed` rows carry `REVIEW-012` condition 2's disclosure, which is RULED and not optional** — the master seed becomes a permanent decryption credential, and the warning for `lsfDisableMaster`, a regular key or a signer list must reach the user **before the seed is asked for**. ⚠ **Issue #10 is open and no code discharges it**: the derivation is specified in one repository document and is not a published standard, so the interface must not imply a holder with their seed and not this repository can reconstruct their key.
   252	
   253	   ⚠⚠ **THE FIRST BUILD VIOLATED THIS STEP'S OWN *"may never touch any private key"*, AND THE GATE COULD NOT SEE IT.** `web/api/issuer.ts` read the issuer secret and decrypted **per request** behind an unauthenticated `GET` — a decryption oracle, and `ADR-0003`'s own fourth rotation trigger, missed by the session that wrote the trigger (`CLAIMS.md` **E-212**). ⚠ **The gate asked what the tier could REACH; this was about what it HELD**, so a **part 4** now checks that no file under `web/` reads a secret environment variable, calls a decryption routine, or spawns a process. **The key lives in `tools/issuer-view-snapshot.ts` and the tier reads its output**, which is what the clause above always said. ⚠ **Two more of the same species**: the API listened on `0.0.0.0` because a bare port number forwards no hostname to `Bun.serve` (**measured on the LAN**), and the browser identity check ran in one loader rather than at the root (**E-213**).
   254	
   255	   *Falsified if:* any file under the web application opens a Unix domain socket, imports a UDS client, or names the signer socket path; or the Elysia process constructs `Request::Pair` or `Request::Prepare`; or any route, loader or server function reaches a signing operation. *Also falsified if:* **any process under `web/` reads a private key, performs a decryption, or spawns a subprocess**, or **the API binds to anything but loopback**. *Also falsified if:* the interface claims a holder is private from the issuer (P-9), presents a freshly-initialised balance as hidden when F-1 says it is publicly known to be exactly zero, describes the custody demo mode as an integration with any custody platform, or emits this project's `tapFailHard` shorthand — which is **not a real name** and has escaped into a public filing once already (E-156).
   256	
   257	9. **The hosted demo — a static, read-only page on a public URL.** **SCOPED 2026-10-19. NOT RULED, NOT BUILT. Round one of its rotation has run (`REVIEW-058`); round two is owed.** `ADR-0004` is the decision record, `Proposed` at revision 2. It carries four decisions for the project owner, D-H1 to D-H4, each priced with a recommendation. ⚠ **A public deployment fires two of step 8's own conditions**: its falsifier *"the API binds to anything but loopback"*, and `ADR-0003`'s trigger 5, egress. The hosted page is public by design, so step 8's loopback property does not carry over to it, and this step's falsifiers replace it.
   258	
   259	   **What the step is, in one sentence, if D-H1 is ruled as recommended:** prerendered static pages, each built from one pinned read of public Devnet state with the reader the local tier already uses, each naming its ledger index and date, with no code of this project running on a server per request and nothing sent by a visitor's browser except page loads to the host. ⚠ **This said the visitor's browser would read Devnet over WebSocket until `REVIEW-058` round one**, which found that reuse failing in a browser and pricing a second reader, and found that revision 1's claim that the gate could enumerate egress was false (`CLAIMS.md` E-328).
   260	
   261	   **It is a second build target, not a replacement.** Step 8's local tier stays as it is. Its signer panel and `/api-doc` page are absent from the hosted build.
   262	
   263	   **What this step may touch:** public Devnet ledger state, read at build time (or, under D-H1's H1, from the visitor's browser over the one named WebSocket endpoint); files built from a clean checkout of the public repository at a named commit, with its locked dependencies, named build variables only and no source maps; and one published issuer snapshot, only if D-H3 rules it.
   264	
   265	   **What it may never touch:** any server-side request handler; any socket client or the signer's socket path; any secret, seed or private key, the demo issuer key included; any decryption routine in the shipped output; any input asking a visitor for a secret; any network but Devnet; any second ledger endpoint, as a fallback or otherwise; any analytics, toolbar or third-party script; and any account a visitor chooses, carried in a URL the host receives.
   266	
   267	   **Its gate is a hosted part of `tools/check-web-readonly.ts`, run over the UPLOADED OUTPUT DIRECTORY and its routing configuration rather than the source**, verified by breaking it in both directions. `ADR-0004` lists what it must check. ⚠ It cannot check egress, and `check-no-secrets` has no directory mode yet, so the scan it relies on does not exist (`REVIEW-058` R1-9).
   268	
   269	   *Falsified if:* the shipped output contains a server function, an API route, a serverless function or middleware, in its files or its routing configuration; or contains a socket client, the signer socket path, a decryption routine or a secret-shaped value; or contains any file the provenance rule does not admit; or asks a visitor for a seed, a key or a secret; or permits a connection to anything but its named targets; or renders a ledger value without the risk wording, the network check and the ledger index it was read at; or renders a failed or negative read that cannot be placed in the pinned ledger as an empty account, or substitutes another source; or carries a visitor's lookup in a URL the host receives; or publishes an issuer figure D-H3 has not ruled; or ships bytes or headers other than the ones the gate passed. *Also falsified if:* any of step 8's wording falsifiers holds on the hosted page.
   270	
   271	## 7. What this architecture must never claim
   272	
   273	Beyond the standing prohibitions in `CLAIMS.md`, which govern:
   274	
   275	- That it hides **who** transacts, with whom, when, or how often. It hides amounts (P-4, P-11).
   276	- That a holder is private from the issuer (P-9).
   277	- That anything is secure, audited, non-custodial or production-ready (P-5).
   278	- That keys can be rotated or recovered (P-10).
   279	- That the local-signer boundary stops an adversary with code execution (§3).
   280	- That a demo of the happy path is evidence of confidentiality. It is not — that is what the observer harness is for.
   281	- **That reading the ledger over TLS makes the ledger data trustworthy.** It authenticates the channel to a node the operator chose. A hostile node substitutes a destination's `HolderEncryptionKey` just as well over TLS, and F-23 says that costs the amount, not the transaction. Added 2026-08-19 with §6 step 2, because the temptation to write "reads the ledger securely" is exactly the shape this list exists to stop.
   282	
   283	## 8. Open questions this document does not answer
   284	
   285	Recorded rather than resolved, so they are not mistaken for settled:
   286	
   287	- ~~**Where the signer's ledger state comes from.** §6 step 2 is not built, so the signer reads sequence numbers, balances, balance versions and other holders' encryption keys from a **profile file** an operator points it at.~~ **ANSWERED 2026-08-19 — it reads the ledger.** The question it turned into is narrower and is **open**: *a signer that read the ledger itself would not need to trust anything local* was true and incomplete — it now trusts **one remote node**, and F-23 says what a lying node costs. `CLAIMS.md` **B-15**: whether corroboration across independent endpoints is required, or whether "the operator chose the node" is the whole answer. Reading the same fields twice is cheap under the existing `LedgerSource` trait and is not built. **Named as a gap, not designed around.**
   288	- ~~**Whether the transaction's ECDSA nonce needs a ruling.**~~ **ANSWERED 2026-08-20 — it did, and it has one** (`REVIEW-018`, B-14 → E-109). ~~What is left open is narrower and is **B-16**: ed25519 is deterministic by construction, it is the live path here, and nobody has ruled on whether that residual is accepted.~~ **B-16 IS RULED TOO, 2026-08-27** (`REVIEW-024`, three legs): the residual is **not** accepted and the nonce prefix is hedged. ~~⚠ **Ruled and not built**~~ — **built and executed the same day (E-163).** What is open is the *second review round*, which reviews round one's fixes.
   289	- ⚠ **Whether issue #10 can be discharged at all inside this project.** Condition 1 asks that the derivation be *published in reproducible detail*, and its benefit — a holder who has the seed and not this binary recovers their key — is real only if the specification is reachable **without this repository**. Three independent implementations now agree on the ruling's prose, which is the best evidence available that it is reimplementable; it is **not** publication. An XLS informational draft is the discharge, and **filing one is a Desktop-project decision**. Recorded here so that "step 6 is built" is never read as "condition 1 is met".
   290	- ⚠ **Who holds the Dedicated Account's key.** `CLAIMS.md` E-117 and ADR-0002 rev 4: rejecting the XLS-65 `Vault` traded away a real property — a `Vault` pseudo-account holds pooled assets **with no key**, and the Dedicated Account replacing it does not. ~~**The facility's whole float therefore sits under one ordinary key, and no review has asked who holds it.**~~ **Answered 2026-09-13:** `REVIEW-046` and `REVIEW-047` asked, and found more holders than one key (the issuer can erase or freeze the float, and the key that decrypts is also required to spend), and the owner ruled B-27: accepted by name, printed on every facility run (`CLAIMS.md` E-290, E-294). Added here on 2026-08-24 because step 7 makes it live rather than theoretical, and because the ADR's own comparison table gained a custody row only after the decision was taken.
   291	- ⚠ **Whether a `fail_hard` submitter that is NOT the signer satisfies B-15's gate.** `REVIEW-019` says *"this signer cannot use it: it does not submit. Whoever submits should."* A separate submitter keeps §1's claim intact and gets the F-23 mitigation — but nothing forces that submitter to set the flag, so the mitigation becomes a convention rather than a property. **That is the question the decision request hands over**, and it is not one of the three options as the ruling stated them.
   292	- **How the signer is distributed**, and the trust that follows. If the issuer builds and ships it, "the operator cannot spend holder funds" becomes "…provided the signer does what it claims." Source distribution and reproducible builds would address it. ADR-0001 names this and does not solve it.
   293	- ~~**Whether the spec requires `r` to be unique** — `CLAIMS.md` B-12, unchecked, and this repo holds no XLS-0096 text.~~ **ANSWERED 2026-08-18 → E-67.** The spec text was obtained; it is **silent**, which makes it a specification gap. The premise that this repo holds no XLS-0096 text was true and is no longer.
   294	- **What the Trail of Bits May 2026 revision audit says.** **Still not obtained, and now known not to be publicly published** (issue #5, `CLAIMS.md` B-13): the Trail of Bits publications repository is current through 2026-08 and holds only the April report. The gap is **bounded** rather than unknown — upstream cites `RIPCTXR-1` (decryption timing, reintroduced) and `RIPCTXR-10` (nonce-KDF IKM framing, Informational) in source, and **neither is keygen or randomness sourcing**, so on present evidence it does not gate any ruling made so far.
   295	- ~~**Whether `rho` must be persisted** across transactions.~~ **STRUCK 2026-08-18 — this was never open, and listing it as open invited a wrong and alarming reading.** It does **not** need to persist, and the reason is the most load-bearing fact in ADR-0001 §(a): the proof links `PC_b` to the on-ledger balance ciphertext **using `sk_A` rather than the historical blinding** (`B₂ − b·G = sk_A·B₁`). Requiring `sk_A` exists *precisely so* the old `ρ` is not needed. `PC_b` is a per-proof commitment, not persistent ledger state. **Executed:** `tools/spike-2026-08-17/send.ts:72` draws a fresh `ρ` on every Send and every one has been accepted — if `ρ` had to persist, none could have been. An adversarial leg read the open question as implying permanent fund loss (REVIEW-011c §2); that is refuted, and the question is closed rather than re-opened.

    20	`S-n | grade | claim | evidence | smallest fix`
    21	
    22	- **S-1 | MEDIUM | The page may never HOLD a secret, but nothing says it may never
    23	  ASK for one.** The may-never-touch list and the gate cover a seed or key in the
    24	  shipped output. A public page carrying this project's name, whose capability
    25	  matrix discusses master seeds, is the obvious shape for a phishing copy, and a
    26	  later page that "tells a visitor how to run the signer locally" (launch plan
    27	  phase 2 step 3) is one careless form away from inviting a paste. | ADR-0004
    28	  *What the hosted surface may touch*; launch plan phase 2 step 3 | Add *"never
    29	  asks a visitor for a seed, key or secret, in any input"* to the never-touch
    30	  list, step 9's falsifier and the gate.
    31	- **S-2 | MEDIUM | The shipped bundle is a distribution of third-party code, and
    32	  its licence notices are priced nowhere.** Phase 1's `NOTICE` and
    33	  `docs/third-party/INVENTORY.md` cover the repository's tracked text. A static
    34	  build ships React, TanStack, `@noble/curves`, `ripple-address-codec` and their
    35	  dependencies as minified code on a public URL, and the MIT and ISC licences
    36	  require their notices to travel with a copy. The ADR calls the output *"the
    37	  static output of the public repository's own source"*, which is also inexact
    38	  for the same reason. | ADR-0004 *Why this shape*; `NOTICE` | Name the bundle's
    39	  notices as a build requirement, and say *"built from the public repository and
    40	  its locked dependencies"*.
    41	- **S-3 | MEDIUM | The host can add script to a page, and the falsifier does not
    42	  name it.** Step 9 is falsified if the page ships bytes other than the gated
    43	  ones, and the never-touch list excludes third-party script. A host that injects
    44	  its own script into some deployments, a preview toolbar for example, would
    45	  violate both without any change of ours. Whether Vercel does this for a
    46	  prebuilt production deployment was **not checked**. | ADR-0004 D-H4; step 9's
    47	  *Falsified if* | Make phase 2 step 5's live check compare the served HTML with
    48	  the gated output, and name host injection as what it is looking for.
    49	- **S-4 | LOW | D-H2's first sentence says more than the design guarantees.**
    50	  *"No amount can be published because of it"* is true of the page, which cannot
    51	  sign. It is not true of a reader who copies a displayed `HolderEncryptionKey`
    52	  into their own tooling: a lying node then reaches F-23 through the reader. |
    53	  ADR-0004 D-H2 | *"Nothing on this page signs or submits. Do not use a value
    54	  shown here to build a transaction."*
    55	- **S-5 | LOW | D-H2's "Do not accept" row implies H3 escapes the acceptance.** H3
    56	  still reads one node, once, at build time, and a lying node then bakes wrong
    57	  values into every page. It changes when the risk is taken, not whether. |
    58	  ADR-0004 D-H2 table | Say H3 moves the read to build time and still needs the
    59	  first sentence.
    60	- **S-6 | LOW | D-H4 option A prices the token as a cost and not as a
    61	  credential.** A Vercel token on the owner's machine can replace what the public
    62	  page says, which is the same kind of power D8 exists to fence for the
    63	  repository. Its scope and expiry are not named. | ADR-0004 D-H4 | Name a token
    64	  scoped to the one project, with an expiry, kept where D8's export folder is.
    65	- **S-7 | LOW | Where the Content Security Policy lives is not said.** For a
    66	  prebuilt static deployment it is either a response header in the build
    67	  output's configuration or a `<meta>` tag, and the two do not support the same
    68	  directives. | ADR-0004 gate list | Say which, and make the gate read the served
    69	  header rather than the source.
    70	- **S-8 | LOW | A visitor cannot tell what built the page.** Nothing on the page
    71	  names the public commit it was built from, so *"ships bytes other than the
    72	  gated ones"* is checkable by the owner and by nobody else. | step 9's

 126 ## Phase 2 — the hosted demo
 127 
 128 ⚠⚠ **This is not a deployment task with a gate attached. It is a trust-boundary
 129 change, and the project's rule is a full adversarial rotation BEFORE implementation.**
 130 Architecture §6 step 8 is *falsified if* *"the API binds to anything but loopback"*
 131 (`ARCHITECTURE-2026-08-18.md:254`), and `ADR-0003`'s trigger 5 fires when any datum
 132 becomes reachable by a party who could not obtain it before. A public deployment is
 133 both. The same tier shipped a decryption oracle once, written by the session that had
 134 just written the trigger (E-212).
 135 
 136 1. **Scope it as its own architecture step** with its own falsifier, and write the ADR
 137    for the hosted surface. The questions it has to answer:
 138    - **What does the hosted tier serve that a public node does not?** Two things are
 139      known: `/api/signer` (signer-local status, including a record count covering
 140      attempts that never reached the ledger) and the decrypted issuer snapshot
 141      (E-228, E-239). ⚠ **Both had already been withdrawn from the local tier on
 142      2026-09-05 (E-241)**, before this plan was written: no route serves the figure,
 143      the record count or the socket path. The hosted design starts from that, and
 144      this note was added on 2026-10-18 (`REVIEW-057` R1-11). The first is removed
 145      from the hosted build. The second is the point of the demo and becomes a deliberately published static artifact over
 146      throwaway Devnet accounts, with the disclosure beside it.
 147    - **The ledger endpoint.** B-15's named risk acceptance was written for a local
 148      operator. A hosted page needs its own wording: a lying source makes the page show
 149      wrong numbers, and nothing signs, so no amount can be published by it.
 150    - **Devnet resets.** The demo accounts are throwaway. When they vanish the page must
 151      say so rather than fall back to another source, which is the substitution
 152      `CLAUDE.md` forbids.
 153    - Abuse, rate limiting and caching, since the endpoint is no longer one operator's.
 154    **Drafted 2026-10-19: `ADR-0004`, `Proposed`, and architecture §6 step 9** (`CLAIMS.md` E-327).
 155    It answers each question above and puts four decisions to the owner, D-H1 to D-H4. The
 156    snapshot sentence in the first question is D-H3 and is not ruled. Under the recommended
 157    hosting shape there is no server, so step 3's CORS item and step 4's request-time checks
 158    change; the ADR says how. Step 2's round one ran the same day (`REVIEW-058`, E-328) and moved
 159    D-H1's recommendation to prerendered pages; round two is owed.
 160 2. **The rotation.** Three legs, differed packets, before implementation.
 161 3. **Build.** A hosted build target that excludes the socket client entirely; CORS for
 162    the deployed origin, which today is a localhost regex; the static issuer snapshot;
 163    a page that tells a visitor how to run the signer locally to transact.
 164 4. **Extend the gate.** `tools/check-web-readonly.ts` asserts the local shape. The
 165    hosted surface needs its own part: zero socket clients in the deployed bundle,
 166    no decryption at request time, and the deployed origin checked against what the
 167    ADR allows. Verify it by breaking it.
 168 5. **Deploy to Vercel and check the live surface** against the ADR's list, from a
 169    machine that has never run the project.
 170 
 171 **Exit:** a live URL that serves public ledger data and one published snapshot,
 172 carries its disclosures on the page, and cannot sign.
